editorial.tldr: China Daily first reported on Aug 6 that DeepSeek planned to raise its AI service prices, and CITIC Securities analysts treated the plan as confirmed days later, framing it as part of a broader trend of Chinese labs pushing larger models at higher prices. By Aug 10, coverage was describing the move as DeepSeek entering a more ambitious, costlier era.
editorial.whats_new: DeepSeek shipped V4-Pro on its API on Aug 13 with sharply higher user prices, confirming the reported hike, and released an open-source coding harness the same day positioned as a Claude Code rival.
editorial.why_it_matters: Teams running production workloads on DeepSeek's API for its low per-token cost should expect that cost advantage to narrow with V4-Pro and re-check budgets before the next bill.
editorial.take_for_builders: Re-check DeepSeek API cost assumptions against V4-Pro's new pricing before it hits production spend, and evaluate whether the new open-source Harness offers a cheaper self-hosted path for coding-agent workloads.

status.detail: Weeks of reports and analyst notes about a coming DeepSeek price increase were confirmed when V4-Pro shipped on the API at sharply higher user prices.
